New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-multicapture-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-multicapture-2026.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-multicapture.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/multicapture`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/multicapture says one PaymentIntent can be captured multiple times up to its authorized amount and lists Stripe-hosted, full embedded and Advanced web routes (new raw lines 5-15). The May 11 full guide explains the IC+ offering and blended-pricing support route, eligible online cards and geography, 50-capture limit, manual capture and the Connect source_transaction restriction (old raw lines 14-35). Hosted and embedded Checkout create a Session whose confirmation creates the PaymentIntent, while Advanced works directly on a PaymentIntent. The merchant requests multicapture with if_available and checks latest_charge status in the eligible manual flow. The server captures a requires_capture PaymentIntent. A non-final partial capture keeps the remaining authorization, and final capture or expiry releases uncaptured authorization. An uncaptured Intent cancels on expiry while a partially captured Intent succeeds on finalization (old raw lines 137-222, old raw lines 364-415, old raw lines 752-938). source-stripe-multicapture.md summarizes the May variants and operational rules. Its existing expiry and zero-capture shorthand at lines 31-35 needs the prior-capture and state distinction independently of the November index.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/multicapture, new raw lines 5-15 preserve the definition and replace detailed variant bodies in the canonical capture with navigation. They do not establish a substantive product change. source-stripe-multicapture.md should retain May 11 conditions for request options, 50 captures, card and geography eligibility, Connect, refunds, webhooks and the manual capture and authorization state boundaries (old raw lines 14-35, old raw lines 137-317, old raw lines 794-1033). The embedded sample omits the documented manual parameter, and in May an automatic or automatic_async request could return available while the Intent was automatically captured in full (old raw lines 329-346, old raw lines 364-415). Warn reciprocally in Stripe Multicapture about both hazards and the distinction between an uncaptured expiry/cancellation, a partially captured Intent becoming succeeded, and the zero-amount release after prior partial capture. The May embedded return-page text equates `complete` with payment success and `open` with failure or cancellation (old raw lines 534-561). The Checkout concept repeats the success shorthand at line 27 even though lines 200-216 distinguish completion from payment. The November Checkout Session API object's lines 312-322 and 368-378 specify separate `status` and `payment_status` fields. Payment may still be processing for `complete`, and `open` is an in-progress Session. Carry this warning in the reciprocal Checkout concept so remount and return-page messaging stay distinct from payment or capture status. In the May guide a PaymentIntent still in `requires_capture` can have already captured funds refunded repeatedly up to `amount_received - amount_refunded`. The Charge object's Boolean `refunded` becomes true only after final capture and refund of the entire amount received. `refund.created` is a separate event documented for each partial refund (old raw lines 234-238, 313-317, 667-671, 746-750, 950-954, 1029-1033). Repair source line 74 from broken `[[stripe-payment-line-items-flexible]]` to existing `[[source-stripe-payment-line-items-flexible]]`. The target's `Multicapture Rules` are at wiki/sources/source-stripe-payment-line-items-flexible.md:15-23, and wiki/concepts/stripe-multicapture.md:67 already uses the correct route. Keep the May migration guide's beta-to-GA header, full-remaining non-final capture error and webhook changes dated to that separate migration context. Neither the November paths nor historical examples establish current merchant access or network compliance.
